lines: Missing pages worry me less than people who never read warnings.
Villages remember more than people expect.
Ink is quiet until someone needs proof.
Records do not care who feels embarrassed by them.
A tidy shelf is proof that peace can be arranged, briefly.
Forgotten warnings do not become kinder. They become <jump>surprises</jump>.
You may prefer I forget. I have chosen a profession that argues otherwise.
I have seen bad sources with more sense than that.
Careful. Even ink looks softer than your manners right now.
The story of me following you needs editing. Mostly shorter chapters and fewer hazards.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
The boat chapter of our journey was damp, brief, and badly footnoted.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
Every village has a history. Some of it even waits politely on shelves.
Books are quiet until you need them. Then they become everyone who wrote before you.
I keep records because memory without witnesses starts bargaining with itself.
